cards.title: A repository
cards.body: A repository (repo) is a project folder that Git keeps track of. `git init` turns the folder you are in into one.
cards.code:
mkdir site
cd site
git init

cards.title: Looking around
cards.body: `ls` lists what is in the folder you are in, `pwd` shows where you are, and `cd` moves into a folder (`cd ..` goes back out).
cards.code:
mkdir demo
cd demo
pwd
touch index.html
ls

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: One command here is not a Git command at all. Tap it.
cards.code:
mkdir notes
cd notes
git int

bug.fix: There is no `git int`. To start a repository, type `git init`.

check.question: Which command turns the current folder into a Git repository?
check.explanation: `git init` creates the hidden `.git` folder where Git keeps its history.

exercise.prompt: Your website's files are in the folder `site`. Go into it with `cd`, then turn it into a Git repository.
